task: T3: document resume and the overrides in docs/ and in the loop's own help. Explain what makes a task "satisfied" — its own gate passing, asked before the executor runs — and why that question is only answerable for a spec with per-task gates, stating plainly that a spec with a single gate is left exactly as it was because a green gate there means the spec is done rather than that any particular task is. Document `RALPH_FORCE_FROM` and `RALPH_FORCE_ALL` with an example of each. Say what this makes possible: an interrupted run can be picked up where it stopped, including an interruption made deliberately to fix a defect in the loop's own gate, which is the case that motivated it. Record the constraint that shapes the rest of the surface — that nothing can connect into a worker, so stop and pause cannot be sent to it and must instead be noticed by it while it polls, the same way a GitHub Actions or GitLab runner discovers cancellation — and note that this spec builds the decisions while the polled source belongs to a later one. Change nothing under `scripts/` except help text.
